newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: China adds to Venezuela oil interests.
newsitem.headline: China adds to Venezuela oil interests.

text.p: China National Petroleum Corp on Tuesday added to its petroleum interests in Venezuela by paying $118 million for a 20-year contract to exploit the Intercampo Norte oilfield in Venezuela's Lake Maracaibo.
Although CNPC's bid was more than double its closest rival, the company's representative Wang Shaoxian said it reflected their geological evaluation of the field's potential.

With 196 million barrels of proven reserves remaining, Petroleos de Venezuela manager Vincenzo Paglione said the bid amounted to 60 cents per barrel of reserves, comparable to fields won on the first day of bidding on Monday.

Current production from the field was 4,200 barrels per day (bpd) of 22 degrees API crude, but this level was falling steadily. Since its discovery in 1954, the field has produced 178 million barrels.
Shaoxian said she was very impressed by the efficiency of Venezuela's state-run Petroleos de Venezuela and would be bidding for more contracts later in the week.

China recently signed a deal to import one million tonnes of Venezuela's bitumen-based boiler fuel Orimulsion this year on a test basis, and Shaoxian said they were hoping to seal a long- term deal this year.
Intercampo Norte was the first contract open to international operators in Venezuela's third round of operating licences. The 20 contracts are being awarded on the basis of cash bids over five days.
